get.description: Serve a cached variant. 404 for an unknown key. Upstream failure (or a disabled proxy) returns **200** with a neutral placeholder PNG and ``X-Art-Fallback`` so an ```` never breaks.
Labels, unsupported pairs and message templates the app's copy tests read.

Reserved for the HEOS yt-dlp bridge (ai-dev #67). The spike verdict is no-go for now:
docs/spikes/ytmusic-heos.md. HEOS sides report YouTube Music as unavailable.

schema.title: Response Metrics Summary Api Metrics Summary Get

applied.title: Applied
applied.description: targets (side or player ids) the command reached

resolved.title: Resolved
resolved.description: transport acks: side id -> the action actually sent (toggle resolved)

latency_ms.title: Latency Ms
latency_ms.description: hub-side time from request to ack

AckWarning.title: AckWarning
AckWarning.description: A non-fatal note about a command that still succeeded (e.g. a second Pandora stream).

AirPlayInfo.title: AirPlayInfo

AirPlayOutput.title: AirPlayOutput
AirPlayOutput.description:
One Music AirPlay device as the app shows it. ``kind`` is Music's raw device kind;
``kind_label`` is the two-way user label the app renders.

ids.title: Ids
ids.description: AirPlay output ids to select (others off)

ArtRef.title: ArtRef
ArtRef.description:
Artwork as served by the hub art proxy (design system §2.2, §11).

``url`` is hub-relative (``/api/art/{cache_key}``); append ``?size=96|320|1080|backdrop``.
``accent`` is the clamped art-derived colour, ``None`` until the proxy has analysed the image.
``accent_is_safe`` is the hub-side contrast check; when false the client uses ``bg-raised``.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: vendor -> null when available, else unsupported | not_linked | not_in_account

Availability.title: Availability
Availability.description:
Which ecosystems can play a service's content, and why not when they cannot.

``reasons[vendor]`` is ``null`` when available, else one of ``unsupported`` (the vendor cannot
play the service at all), ``not_linked`` (the vendor app lacks the service link) or
``not_in_account`` (Pandora: the station is not in that vendor's account). The router's
messages remain the copy of record; the app uses the reason to pick the sentence before a
tap (``GET /api/meta/messages``).

Capabilities.title: Capabilities
Capabilities.description:
What a player or side can do, so Phase 1 does not hard-code vendor checks.

``supports_next`` / ``supports_prev`` follow the current source (HEOS ``supported_controls``,
Sonos DIDL item class): a radio station has no next track.

Container.title: Container
Container.description: An album or playlist with its tracks.

ContentRef.title: ContentRef
ContentRef.description:
Canonical service id: what the hub browses by and plays from ("browse once, play
anywhere", PRD review §2.1). Also the cross-vendor identity of the current track.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: Bare error envelope shape (non-command routes) for OpenAPI ``responses``.

art_cache.title: Art Cache
art_cache.description: entries, bytes, hits, misses; null when the proxy is off

last_targets.title: Last Targets
last_targets.description: side ids of the last play

needs_link.title: Needs Link
needs_link.description: hub-linked services that contribute to this section and are currently unlinked (e.g. ['tidal']); items from every linked service still render

linked.title: Linked
linked.description: per-source linkage: library sections map service -> true | false | null (browse errored); the stations section maps vendor -> true | false | null (unknown)

PandoraSyncStartBody.title: PandoraSyncStartBody
PandoraSyncStartBody.description:
Exactly one of ``side_ids`` (rooms; the hub matches their names to outputs) or
``output_ids`` (explicit AirPlay outputs).

PandoraSyncState.title: PandoraSyncState
PandoraSyncState.description:
Experimental "Pandora Sync" via the hub Mac as an AirPlay 2 sender (PRD §3.5 PAN-4).

The hub only routes AirPlay outputs and opens Pandora on the Mac; playback itself is driven
there (docs/spikes/airplay-bridge.md). ``previous_output_ids`` is what ``stop`` restores;
``side_ids`` are the rooms whose outputs are bridged, so the app can scope its controls.

PlayMode.title: PlayMode
PlayMode.description:
Shuffle / repeat as the coordinator reports it (Phase 8, ai-dev #79).

HEOS: ``player/get_play_mode`` → ``repeat`` ∈ on_all|on_one|off and ``shuffle`` on|off.
Sonos: ``PlayMode`` ∈ NORMAL|SHUFFLE_NOREPEAT|SHUFFLE|REPEAT_ALL|REPEAT_ONE|SHUFFLE_REPEAT_ONE.
Both map onto the same two fields here.

QueueEntry.title: QueueEntry
QueueEntry.description: One track in a side's native queue, in the shape the client renders (ai-dev #77).

QueueState.title: QueueState
QueueState.description: A side's queue as last read from the coordinator; streamed as ``queues.<side>``.

SyncConfig.title: SyncConfig
SyncConfig.description: Hot-reloadable tuning (``POST /api/sync/config``). Defaults come from settings.

heos_target.title: Heos Target
heos_target.description: HEOS player id, side id, or a list of player ids (grouped first)

sonos_target.title: Sonos Target
sonos_target.description: Sonos player id, side id, or a list of player ids (grouped first)

SyncState.title: SyncState

Zone.title: Zone
Zone.description: A Denon amplifier zone, namespaced by receiver host: ``denon-{host}:{key}``.

zone_id.title: Zone Id
zone_id.description: Denon zone id, or a Sonos player/side id for stop+ungroup
